decisionSource: The release owner explicitly approved the named human dispositions, scope, expiries, and compensating controls in the implementation session on 2026-09-21.

acceptances.rationale: The broader initiative supplies the missing matrix and preserves the original review boundary.
controls: Preserve the complete candidate matrix and narrow review boundary in retained release evidence.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: ADR 0001 makes this a durable test-design constraint.
controls: Keep the ADR-backed lifecycle test design and regression evidence release-gated.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: This is an intentional sampling contract, not evidence of durable acknowledgement.
controls: Document sampling as observability-only and keep acknowledgement correctness in adapter evidence.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: The distinction is a documented semantic boundary.
controls: Keep the semantic boundary documented and covered by exact metrics and health fixtures.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: Serial processing and the absence of a DLQ producer remain explicit boundaries. The prior lack of cooperative-rebalance fencing is remediated when callers install kafkaRebalanceHandler; live two-consumer evidence proves the old owner's callback is rejected.
controls: Document serial processing and missing DLQ production, and require the rebalance fencing helper where cooperative rebalancing is used.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: Live buffered-retry, restart, idle-shutdown, and repeated-shutdown cases preserve the documented close-time commit contract without skipping unresolved work.
controls: Retain live buffered-retry, restart, idle-shutdown, and repeated-shutdown evidence for each candidate.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: Ephemeral PostgreSQL restart preserves the same durable message identity, which becomes readable after the configured visibility lease expires; delayed availability remains the documented at-least-once contract.
controls: Document visibility-timeout delayed redelivery and retain live durable-identity restart evidence.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: At-least-once replay is an intentional checkpoint contract.
controls: Document at-least-once replay and retain per-delivery restart evidence for Kiroku.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: This is positive historical evidence with an explicitly narrow scope.
controls: Do not generalize historical evidence beyond its recorded candidate and lifecycle boundary.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: The MasterPlan explicitly preserves the narrow approval boundary.
controls: Keep the approval boundary explicit in the MasterPlan and release verdict.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: This is a runtime boundary that must be documented rather than hidden.
controls: Document the uninterruptible-user-code boundary and retain bounded-shutdown regression coverage.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: The bounded overshoot is documented design behavior.
controls: Keep bounded overshoot documented and covered by the keyed-concurrency reference model.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: The 0.10.x release documents the measured finite-range memory envelope and requires callers to bound caller-controlled distinct batch-key cardinality. This is a time- and version-bounded residual-risk acceptance, not a claim that the implementation enforces a key limit.
controls: Callers bound caller-controlled distinct in-progress batch-key cardinality.
Release documentation states the observed upper envelope of 703 bytes per additional key over the tested 1,000-to-50,000-key range.
Reopen REV-15-L1 before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.

acceptances.rationale: The two tests prove distinct ownership states.
controls: Retain both ownership-state regression tests and process-isolated GC coverage.
Reopen this acceptance before 0.11.0.0 or after the calendar expiry, whichever occurs first.
